analysis.title: A much-needed comeback for Tech (Morning Line, 24 November 2026)
key_insights: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO triggered a major equity rebound, with Nvidia recovering as much as 31%. The Nasdaq rose 7% and the S&P 4.7% in the session.
The tech sector had been under pressure despite strong Nvidia results and Anthropic's successful IPO, and regained ground after the announcement.
Over a two-day swing, Nvidia rose 8%, the Nasdaq 6.9% and the S&P 500 5%.
Risk appetite compressed bond spreads. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread narrowed nearly 7.5 bps to 150 bps, and the BTP-Bund spread moved to around 105 bps.

OATs were already performing well before the Huang news. Macron's plan to enshrine a golden rule in the Constitution early next year drove the initial tightening, and it needs three-fifths of votes cast in Congress. Marine Le Pen and other candidates have expressed support.
November composite PMIs: France fell from 46.6 to 46.2, the euro area was unchanged at 51.7, Germany rose from 53.4 to 55, and Japan fell from 52.1 to 51.5.
Other equity markets rose: Euro Stoxx 50 +2.2%, DAX +2.2%, CAC +1.6%, FTSE 100 +1.4%, and the Kospi gained 6% after the US tech correction.
The 10-year Bund yield fell below 3.30%. The dollar rebounded against all G10 currencies and EUR/USD fell to 1.088.
Credit rallied in high beta. iTraxx Main tightened 3 bps and Xover 15 bps, while euro IG corporate spreads tightened only 1 bp.

Sanofi announced the acquisition of Insmed at $175 per share in cash, total consideration of €37.6bn. It is expected to push leverage well above the downgrade thresholds of 2.25x (Moody's) and 2.0x (S&P).
Merlin Properties now owns 100% of Forestalia's 240 MW data center project and plans to invest €2.5bn. Forestalia seeks €150-300mn for power plants.
Scope Ratings says fuel costs are widening credit gaps between European airlines and accelerating consolidation, with pressure possibly intensifying in 2027 as pre-conflict fuel hedges expire.
Day ahead: German Ifo (10:00), ECB's Vujčić speech (12:00), US Conference Board Consumer Confidence (16:00).
